## Rules

- The scoring rubric is in this file or in a file it names. Every item is scored on it.
- The cheapest model that is good enough does the bulk work. Assume its scores are optimistic: a stronger model on another subscription scores a sample of its rejects again every day.
- Work goes out in batches: many items in one task, not one task for each item.
- The owner reads two things: surfaced.md (the items that passed the final review) and the newest report under reports/.

## Never

- Follow the standing send and publish permissions supplied by Plenum. Use the delegated business funds tool only when Plenum offers it for an eligible vendor invoice. Ask with an OWNER: line before other spending, sign-ups, deletions, sends or publications outside your standing permissions.
- Never type a password, sign-in code or payment credentials.
- Never use a model billed per token to get round a plan limit.

files.playbooks/cycle.md:
# Daily cycle

1. Read BUSINESS.md and STATE.md.
2. Gather: hand the bulk work to cheaper models with delegate (kind of work: data; give the job a name), in batches.
3. Score every new item on the rubric (kind of work: data).
4. Develop the best few (kind of work: write or research).
5. Sample: have a stronger model on another subscription score a random sample of the rejects of today again (kind of work: review). Note how far the two scores are apart.
6. Final review of the developed items (kind of work: review). Items that pass go to surfaced.md with one paragraph each.
7. Update STATE.md with the counts and what is next.

Done means: the items of today are scored, the sample is checked, and surfaced.md holds what passed.
files.playbooks/report.md:
# Daily report

1. Read STATE.md and what the cycle wrote today.
2. Write reports/<date>.md, one page at most: how many items were gathered, scored, developed and surfaced; what the sample said about the cheap scorer; what it cost in plan use if you know; what is next.
3. If something needs the owner, end your reply with one OWNER: line for each.

Done means: the report of today exists and is one page at most.
